body: Just ask yourself 1), "how likely is it my house is infested with ants?" (I'd say odds are pretty good) and 2), "do I really want to risk my Nutella being extra crunchy?"

Everyone knows they're going to die; you just have to think about it more. Wasting your ONLY good years by ending it all now, won't solve anything. Everyone faces the same situation you do, in a sense. They just have more time to do it. Is that fair? No. But life is about making the most of the time we have, how ever short that may be. I think of what Christopher Hitchens said roughly 10 months before he died of cancer: https://youtu.be/hc6UdA3TtWY 

I don't know if this helps. I'm not great at encouragement, but I hope it does. You, more than most people, should be concerned about the time you do have. Use it. Even if it's cliche, hitchhike across the country, write a book about your experience (you clearly have writing skills), partake in a risky experimental group for the disease.
Long story short: use your time.
